ref: [37] P. Chen, J. Gong, T. Chen, Accuracy can lie: On the impact of surrogate model in configuration tuning, IEEE TSE 51(2), 2025; [83] Chen, Liang & Chen arXiv:2509.21945

target_raw: SE optimization needs its own optimizers (Agrawal et al.)
evidence: SE optimization has certain features which require special kinds of optimizers [54]. ... the optimizer that wins in ML may not win here [54].
ref: [54] A. Agrawal et al., Simpler hyperparameter optimization for software analytics: Why, how, when?, IEEE TSE 48(8), 2021, pp. 2939-2954.

target_raw: Few labels suffice on 2^460 space (Rayegan & Menzies)
evidence: with just 50 labels (0.5% of the data) the methods used in this paper can reach 80% of optimal [1].
ref: [1] A. Rayegan and T. Menzies, Minimal data, maximum clarity, JSS 2026.

evidence: our tournament and replication package are open-sourced for SBSE researchers and practitioners at https://github.com/KKGanguly/OptimizerTournament.
ref: https://github.com/KKGanguly/OptimizerTournament

evidence: NSGA-II [9] is the one of the most widely cited multi-objective evolutionary algorithm in SBSE [5]... Both are run at 200 (equal-budget comparison) and 1000 evaluations
ref: [9] Deb, Pratap, Agarwal, Meyarivan. A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II. IEEE Trans. Evo. Comp., 6(2):182-197, 2002.

evidence: SPEA2 [10] provides an archive-based alternative with strength fitness and k-NN density estimation. Including both ensures results are not artifacts of NSGA-II's specific crowding-distance mechanism.
ref: [10] Zitzler, Laumanns, Thiele. SPEA2: Improving the strength Pareto evolutionary algorithm. TIK-Report 103, ETH Zurich, 2001.

evidence: SMAC [11] fits a Random Forest surrogate over the decision space and uses Expected Improvement to select evaluations, optimising D2H directly.
ref: [11] Hutter, Hoos, Leyton-Brown. Sequential model-based optimization for general algorithm configuration. Proc. LION, pages 507-523. Springer, 2011.

target_canonical: Random search baseline (Bergstra & Bengio; Arcuri & Briand)
evidence: Arcuri and Briand [25] demonstrated that random search often provides surprisingly competitive performance in SBSE, making it an essential baseline for any optimization comparison.
ref: [25] Arcuri, Briand. A practical guide for using statistical tests to assess randomized algorithms in software engineering. ICSE, pages 1-10. IEEE, 2011.

evidence: We use a minimal contrastive regional search, EZR [13, 14]. It maintains a Best set (sqrt N solutions with lowest D2H found so far) and a Rest set
ref: [13] Rayegan, Menzies. Minimal data, maximum clarity: A heuristic for explaining optimization. arXiv:2509.08667, 2025. [14] Menzies, Ganguly. How low can you go? 2026.

evidence: Replication package: https://github.com/kkganguly/ParetoMyth.
ref: https://github.com/kkganguly/ParetoMyth

evidence: We evaluate on MOOT (Multi-Objective Optimization Testing) [4], a repository consolidating over 100 SE optimization tasks drawn from dozens of peer-reviewed publications
ref: [4] Menzies, Chen, Ye, Ganguly, Rayegan, Srinivasan, Lustosa. Moot: a repository of many multi-objective optimization tasks. arXiv:2511.16882, 2025.

target_raw: Scott-Knott recursive bi-clustering (with bootstrap + Cliff's delta)
evidence: We perform statistical comparisons via Scott-Knott recursive bi-clustering method [47]. It clusters optimizers per dataset by recursively splitting ranked distributions only where bootstrap significance and Cliff's Delta effect size both confirm
ref: [47] A. J. Scott and M. Knott. A cluster analysis method for grouping means in the analysis of variance. Biometrics, 30:507-512, 1974.

evidence: Win/Tie/Loss counts follow the pairwise practice recommended by Demsar [48]: the cheaper method is the reference
ref: [48] Janez Demsar. Statistical comparisons of classifiers over multiple data sets. JMLR, 7(Jan):1-30, 2006.

target_raw: Distance-to-ideal / equal-weight aggregation (Hwang & Yoon; Zeleny) -> D2H metric
evidence: equal-weight aggregation is the theoretically grounded default, and the recommended first point to inspect is the solution closest to the ideal [19, 20]... We therefore use Distance-to-Heaven (D2H)
ref: [19] Hwang, Yoon. Multiple attribute decision making. Springer, 2012. [20] Zeleny. Multiple Criteria Decision Making. McGraw-Hill, 1982.

target_raw: IGD/HV Pareto evaluation guidance (Li, Chen & Yao)
evidence: Li et al. [21] provide standard evaluation guidance using IGD and HV, which our RQ3 follows.
ref: [21] Miqing Li, Tao Chen, Xin Yao. How to evaluate solutions in pareto-based search-based software engineering? A critical review and methodological guidance. IEEE TSE, 2020.

evidence: The decision-tree explainability step builds on Rayegan and Menzies [13], which show that shallow Best-vs.-Rest trees produce actionable configuration guidance
ref: [13] Amirali Rayegan and Tim Menzies. Minimal data, maximum clarity: A heuristic for explaining optimization. arXiv:2509.08667, 2025.

target_raw: Prior MOOT benchmark of SMAC vs TPE/DEHB (Menzies & Ganguly)
evidence: A prior study on the same MOOT benchmark [14] found it competitive with or better than TPE [23] and DEHB [24], making it a reasonable choice among global Bayesian methods
ref: [14] Tim Menzies and Kishan Kumar Ganguly. How low can you go? The data-light SE challenge. Arxiv, 2026.

evidence: population sizes of 10 and 20 for 200 and 1000 evaluation budgets were used respectively, following evidence that smaller populations with more generations improve performance [49]
ref: [49] Max Hort and Federica Sarro. The effect of offspring population size on NSGA-II: A preliminary study. GECCO, pages 1-2. ACM, 2021.

target_canonical: SS-* config datasets / FLASH (Nair et al.)
target_raw: Evaluation-cost evidence from FLASH (Nair et al.)
evidence: compiler flag selection requires 35-135 minutes per evaluation [16], and Nair et al. explicitly note that exploring more than a handful of configurations is usually infeasible
ref: [16] Vivek Nair, Zhe Yu, Tim Menzies, Norbert Siegmund, Sven Apel. Finding faster configurations using FLASH. IEEE TSE, 46(7):794-811, 2020.

evidence: similarly, expert elicitation yields roughly ten labels per session [17, 18]. In such settings ... cap realistic budgets well below 1,000 evaluations
ref: [17] Valerdi. Heuristics for systems engineering cost estimation. IEEE Sys. J., 2010. [18] Easterby-Smith. The design, analysis and interpretation of repertory grids. IJMMS 13(1), 1980.

target_raw: Pareto-vs-weighted SBSE study (Chen & Li) - baseline selection and population assumptions
evidence: NSGA-II and SPEA2 were selected as the most widely used Pareto methods in SBSE [7], reflecting standard community practice.
ref: [7] J. Chen and M. Li. The weights can be harmful: Pareto search versus weighted search in multi-objective SBSE. ACM TOSEM, 32:1-40, 2023.

evidence: As per Colanzi et al., it is the second most widely used optimizers in SBSE over the past decade [22].
